examples.note: А and а are the same letter in two print cases.
Б and б are the same letter in two print cases.
Printed pair В в. Treat the Cyrillic identity, not a Latin look-alike.
М and м are the same letter in two print cases.
Printed pair Н н. Treat the Cyrillic identity, not a Latin look-alike.
Printed pair Р р. Treat the Cyrillic identity, not a Latin look-alike.
Printed pair С с. Treat the Cyrillic identity, not a Latin look-alike.
Printed pair У у. Treat the Cyrillic identity, not a Latin look-alike.
Printed pair Х х. Treat the Cyrillic identity, not a Latin look-alike.

items.prompt: Which printed letter is shown?
items.feedback: The printed shape can match Latin A. In this course it is the Cyrillic vowel letter А.

items.prompt: Which printed letter is shown?
items.feedback: М is an early consonant letter. It is not Н.

items.prompt: This letter looks like Latin P. What is it?
items.feedback: Shape overlap with Latin P is a recognition trap. This is Cyrillic Р, not English P.

items.prompt: This letter looks like Latin H. What is it?
items.feedback: Do not read Н as English H. It is a Cyrillic letter.

items.prompt: This letter looks like Latin C. What is it?
items.feedback: С is a Cyrillic letter. Do not treat the Latin look-alike as the identity.

items.prompt: This letter looks like Latin B. What is it?
items.feedback: В is not Latin B and it is not Cyrillic Б.

items.prompt: This letter looks like Latin Y. What is it?
items.feedback: У is a Cyrillic vowel letter, not Latin Y.

items.prompt: This letter looks like Latin X. What is it?
items.feedback: Х is a Cyrillic letter, not Latin X.

items.prompt: Which printed letter is shown?
items.feedback: Ё is its own letter. Е and Э are different letters.

items.prompt: Which printed letter is shown?
items.feedback: Ю is an iotated vowel letter. У and Я are different letters.

items.prompt: Which printed letter is shown?
items.feedback: Я is an iotated vowel letter. It is not Р or А.

items.prompt: What is the printed letter Й?
options: A consonant letter, not a vowel
items.answer: A consonant letter, not a vowel
items.feedback: Й is not a vowel you read alone and it is not the soft sign.

items.prompt: Which line is one letter written in both print cases?
items.feedback: А / а is one letter. The other lines are two different letters.

items.prompt: Which printed letter is shown?
items.feedback: Е is an iotated vowel letter. Э and Ё are different letters.

items.prompt: What is the printed mark Ь?
options: A vowel you pronounce by itself
A mark, not a standalone vowel
items.answer: A mark, not a standalone vowel
items.feedback: Ь is a sign, not a vowel letter you read alone.

items.prompt: What is the printed mark Ъ?
options: The hard sign, not a vowel
items.answer: The hard sign, not a vowel
items.feedback: Ъ is the hard sign. It is not a spoken vowel and it is not Ь.

items.prompt: Which pair is the same letter in uppercase and lowercase print?
items.feedback: Print pairs are one letter in two cases. Р / п and Н / и are different letters.

items.prompt: This letter looks like Latin B. What is it?
items.feedback: В is not Latin B and it is not Cyrillic Б.

items.prompt: This letter looks like Latin Y. What is it?
items.feedback: У is a Cyrillic vowel letter, not Latin Y.

items.prompt: This letter looks like Latin X. What is it?
items.feedback: Х is a Cyrillic letter, not Latin X.

items.prompt: Which pair is the same letter in uppercase and lowercase print?
items.feedback: Б / б is one letter. В is a different letter.

items.prompt: Which printed letter is shown?
items.feedback: Я is an iotated vowel letter. It is not Р or А.

references.title: Cyrillic print forms
references.detail: Use the letter board grouped by the Unit 1 sequence. English sound notes are pending review. No example words are attached.

references.title: Confusable Latin look-alikes
references.summary: В Н Р С У Х can be misread by Latin-alphabet readers.
references.detail: Name the Cyrillic identity. Confirm sounds in your book.

references.title: Iotated vowel letters
references.summary: Е Ё Ю Я are a recognition group in Unit 1.
references.detail: Detailed phonetics remain in the book until a reviewer signs an app note.

references.title: Soft sign, hard sign, and Й
references.summary: Ь and Ъ are signs. Й is not a standalone vowel in this foundation.
references.detail: Do not invent a spoken vowel for the signs. Use the book for the exact rule.
searchTerms: soft sign, hard sign, and й

references.title: Transliteration is temporary
references.summary: Latin respelling may help the first hours. It is not how you should keep reading.
references.detail: Turn transliteration off in settings as soon as print recognition is stable.

references.title: Staged decoding limits
references.summary: This pack decodes letters and print pairs only.
references.detail: Word, phrase, and sign reading wait for reviewed examples.

references.title: Stress notation
references.summary: Stress is part of Russian reading and is not guessed by the app.
references.detail: Copy stress marks from your book into your binder.

references.title: Pronunciation guidance
references.summary: Model audio is used only when a file is licensed and mapped to the current objective.
references.detail: User recordings play at original speed. No ASR or score.

references.title: How to use this companion
references.summary: The app coordinates the book, optional AnkiDroid, a binder, and optional tutor work.
references.detail: It does not reproduce Penguin, judge spontaneous speech, or certify proficiency.

references.title: App limitations
references.summary: Offline only. No internet, no account, no AI, no cloud.
references.detail: Unrelated catalog audio is not assigned to Units 1–2. The app does not score handwriting or pronunciation. Handwriting study uses your book until verified images exist. Unit 2 reviews Unit 1 letters and does not teach Lesson 3 grammar. Public release stays blocked until review and device evidence exist.

units.title: Learning to read Russian
units.topicSummary: Content-complete development unit for printed letters: identities, print pairs, look-alikes, signs, and letter-level decoding. Qualified review and the owned-edition mapping are still pending.
units.mappingNote: Proposed Lesson 1 mapping from the publisher's public table of contents. Owned-edition comparison is not signed, so this unit is not labeled aligned.

objectives.title: Separate Cyrillic letters from Latin look-alikes
Recognize Е Ё Ю Я as a group
Treat Ь Ъ Й as non-ordinary-vowel letters
Match uppercase and lowercase print pairs
Confirm letter sounds in the book
Treat stress as book-marked, not guessed
Complete Lesson 1 work in the owned book

steps.title: Unit 1 — Printed letters
steps.body: This is a proposed Lesson 1 mapping, not an approved owned-edition alignment. The development unit teaches printed letter identities with public-domain letter forms. Example words and model audio are not part of this unit. Qualified review is still pending.
steps.bookDirection: Open your copy to Lesson 1. Use the book for the author's explanations, exercises, and any example words.

steps.title: Identify letters first
steps.body: Work letter shapes, print pairs, and Latin look-alikes before later reading. Transliteration, if you use it, is a temporary support.

steps.title: Cyrillic is a different alphabet
steps.body: Russian is written with 33 Cyrillic letters. Some printed shapes look like Latin letters and are not the same letters. Learn identity first.

steps.title: First vowel set
steps.body: Work these printed pairs: А а, О о, У у, Э э, Ы ы, И и. English sound notes are pending qualified review.

steps.title: Identify А
steps.body: Choose the Cyrillic identity for the printed letter.

steps.title: Low-confusion consonants
steps.body: Next printed pairs: М м, Т т, К к, П п, Б б, Д д, Г г. Confirm each spoken sound in your book. This unit does not play model audio.

steps.title: Identify М
steps.body: Choose the Cyrillic identity for the printed letter.

steps.title: Shape traps
steps.body: These printed letters often fool Latin-alphabet readers: В, Н, Р, С, У, Х. Name the Cyrillic identity.

steps.title: Р is not P
steps.body: Identity check.

steps.title: Н is not H
steps.body: Identity check.

steps.title: С is not C
steps.body: Identity check.

steps.title: В, У, and Х
steps.body: Identity check for the remaining look-alikes.

steps.title: Е Ё Ю Я
steps.body: Recognize these printed forms as a group. Exact phonetics belong in your book.

steps.title: Identify Е, Ё, Ю, and Я
steps.body: Identity check.

sessions.title: Soft sign, hard sign, and Й

steps.title: Marks that are not ordinary vowels
steps.body: Ь, Ъ, and Й need special attention. Do not invent a spoken vowel for the signs.

steps.title: Soft sign
steps.body: Identity check.

steps.title: Hard sign
steps.body: Identity check.

steps.title: Й is not a vowel
steps.body: Identity check.

steps.title: Uppercase and lowercase together
steps.body: Every letter has a print pair. Match them on the letter board. Handwritten forms wait for verified assets.

steps.title: Match a print pair
steps.body: Identity check.

steps.title: Decode print pairs
steps.body: Name the letter, then match its uppercase and lowercase print forms. This unit does not introduce words.
steps.bookDirection: Use the elementary reading work in your Lesson 1 pages for anything beyond a single letter.

steps.title: One letter, two cases
steps.body: Choose the line that is a single letter.

steps.title: Confirm sounds in your book
steps.body: This unit does not play model audio. Use the pronunciation notes in your book for each new letter. A recording you make is stored and is not scored.
steps.bookDirection: Read the Lesson 1 pronunciation notes in the edition you own.

steps.title: Stress is part of reading
steps.body: Russian word stress is not predictable from spelling alone. Marked example words are not installed.
steps.bookDirection: When your Lesson 1 pages mark stress, copy that mark into your binder.

steps.title: Lesson 1 in your copy
steps.body: Complete the Lesson 1 reading and pronunciation work in the edition you own.
steps.bookDirection: Read and do Lesson 1 in your book. Use the book's answer key, not this app, for book exercises.
steps.companionDirection: Afterward, mark book work complete as a self-attestation. That is not demonstrated in-app ability.

steps.title: AnkiDroid if you use it
steps.body: If you selected AnkiDroid, make cards only from material you are allowed to use.
steps.companionDirection: Self-attest AnkiDroid work. It remains user-reported.

steps.title: One useful binder note
steps.body: Write one confusable letter pair that tricked you and the identity you will trust next time.
steps.companionDirection: A binder prompt is a specific note, not 'take notes.'

steps.title: Optional tutor
steps.body: Tutor work is optional for default advancement.

steps.title: Letter identities
steps.body: Revisit any missed letter, then open the explanation it names.

units.title: Handwriting and additional pronunciation
units.topicSummary: Content-complete development unit after Unit 1: printed-letter review, then book-directed handwriting and additional pronunciation. Verified handwriting images and mapped pronunciation audio are not in this app. Qualified review and the owned-edition mapping are still pending.
units.mappingNote: Proposed Lesson 2 mapping from the publisher's public table of contents: handwriting recognition and additional pronunciation. Owned-edition comparison is not signed, so this unit is not labeled aligned.

objectives.title: Complete Lesson 2 work in the owned book

steps.title: Unit 2 — Book handwriting and letter review
steps.body: Proposed Lesson 2 continues handwritten forms and pronunciation in the book. This unit reviews printed letters from Unit 1. Verified handwriting images and mapped pronunciation audio are not in the app, so those parts stay in the book you own.
steps.bookDirection: Open Lesson 2 in your copy for handwritten forms and the author's pronunciation notes.

steps.title: Handwritten forms stay in the owned book
steps.body: Verified handwriting images are not in this app. Use Lesson 2 in the book you own to see handwritten forms, and copy them onto paper. This app does not describe those forms and does not grade the page.
steps.bookDirection: Copy the handwritten forms from Lesson 2 in your book onto paper. This app does not show or grade them.

steps.title: Keep letter identities available
steps.body: Review the printed letters from Unit 1, especially Latin look-alikes and print pairs.

steps.title: Match the printed pair for Б
steps.body: Choose the uppercase and lowercase print pair for the same letter.

steps.title: В is not B
steps.body: Identity check.

steps.title: У is not Y
steps.body: Identity check.

steps.title: Х is not X
steps.body: Identity check.

steps.title: Additional pronunciation stays in the owned book
steps.body: No licensed pronunciation audio is mapped to Unit 2. Use the Lesson 2 pronunciation notes in the book you own. This app does not state those sounds and does not score a recording.
steps.bookDirection: Use the Lesson 2 pronunciation notes in your copy. Model audio is not in this app.

steps.title: Read what the book provides
steps.body: Fluency practice in this unit is book-directed. Re-run letter recognition if a form is still slow.
steps.bookDirection: Read the Lesson 2 material in your copy aloud. Mark difficult letters for review.

steps.title: Optional recording without a score
steps.body: You may record yourself reading from your book. Play the take back. The app never transcribes or scores it.

steps.title: Lesson 2 in your copy
steps.body: Complete Lesson 2 handwriting and pronunciation work in the edition you own. Self-attest when finished.
steps.bookDirection: Do Lesson 2 in your book, including handwritten-form practice.

steps.title: Reviewed letter identities
steps.body: Closed-response items about printed letters from Unit 1.
